name: Prompt-anchored ToMe diagnostic on PolypGen seq5
status: design frozen; helper and real-frame gate implemented; both await execution after the active cohort run
purpose: Mechanism diagnostic for whether a fixed prompt object pointer is a more useful token-matching reference than the current source frame's pointer during prolonged SAM2 presence failures.

scope.role: post-hoc development diagnostic only; not an efficacy cohort or independent confirmation
scope.prompt: Use the sequence's original frame-0 prompt unchanged.
scope.frames: Propagate all 249 post-prompt targets in order; no hand-picked target frames.

method.matching: For every stored spatial memory token, compute cosine affinity to the object pointer from the earliest fixed conditioning frame; append this scalar to the existing normalized mean-head post-RoPE key matching metric.
method.merge: Reuse the pinned ToMe bipartite matcher, weighted K/V merge, and log cluster-mass attention bias from modeling/pointer_conditioned_tome.py.

required_real_frame_gate_before_seq5_rep: fixed prompt-pointer identity across source frames
no evaluation-mask access by matching code
verification.runner_integration_status: not built; the gate script only performs bounded engineering replay

report.primary_diagnostic: per-frame object-score logit and unsuppressed/suppressed mask behavior on all frames, with GT used only after inference for offline analysis
report.claim_limit: Any improvement on seq5 is exploratory because this sequence informed the method. It cannot support a cohort or generalization claim. No full-cohort rerun is authorized by this protocol.

execution.blocked_until: PID 50946 full-cohort pointer-conditioned ToMe run is complete and its frozen results are audited
